01 Honest Run.goal: Establish the reference behaviour with no faults: how far the confirmed and finalized checkpoints run behind the head.
01 Honest Run.result: The confirmed tip runs one slot behind the head. Each node holds up to k = 4 live locks. The finalized checkpoint runs 16–24 slots behind: one finality height per 8-slot round, finalized two rounds after its target.

02 Partition 50/50.goal: See what an even network split does to confirmations, locks and finality, and how the network heals.
02 Partition 50/50.setup: 4 nodes, 64 honest validators, 200 ms latency. Nodes 0–1 and 2–3 are cut apart for slots 48–63.
02 Partition 50/50.result: Each half confirms and fast-locks its own branch (32 votes, exactly n/2). Neither reaches the quorum of 43, so finality stalls. At the heal every lock has exactly 32 opponents and moves back: every block of the cut is discarded on both sides (hollow dots). Heads agree at once and finality resumes within two rounds.

03 Partition 75/25.goal: See whether the majority side of an uneven split notices it, and how the minority recovers.
03 Partition 75/25.setup: 4 nodes, 64 honest validators, 200 ms latency. Nodes 0–2 (48 validators) and node 3 (16) are cut apart for slots 48–63.
03 Partition 75/25.result: The majority keeps confirming, fast-locking and finalizing as if nothing happened. The minority confirms its own blocks and slow-locks them after k = 4 confirmations. At the heal the majority's votes unlock the minority, which reorgs onto the majority chain (depth 3).

04 Partition 52/48.goal: See which side wins when a split leaves one side just above n/2 and the other just below.
04 Partition 52/48.setup: 4 nodes, 64 honest validators, 200 ms latency. 33 validators are cut from the other 31 for slots 48–63.
04 Partition 52/48.result: Only the 33-side passes the fast test (66 ≥ 64). At the heal its locks have 31 opponents, fewer than n/2, and survive; the 31-side's locks have 33 and move back. The larger side's branch wins and the other side reorgs (depth 7).

05 Long Partition 50/50.goal: Check whether a long even split heals as fast as the short one of tab 02.
05 Long Partition 50/50.setup: 4 nodes, 64 honest validators, 200 ms latency. Nodes 0–1 and 2–3 are cut apart for 64 slots (48–111).
05 Long Partition 50/50.result: Each node discards 28–35 confirmed blocks and finality stalls for 8 rounds. Healing is still immediate: no lock survives the heal, and finality resumes after it.

06 Messy Heal.goal: Check healing when the messages held back by a split arrive at random times instead of all at once (tab 02).
06 Messy Heal.setup: 4 nodes, 64 honest validators, 200 ms latency. A 50/50 cut for slots 48–63; the held messages are released at random times up to 12 s (2 slots) after the heal.
06 Messy Heal.result: Heads and confirmed tips agree within about three slots of the last delivery. The same holds across 320 seeded runs of this kind, far inside the spec's healing bound.

07 One-Slot Glitch at a Round Start.goal: Check whether a single bad slot at the start of a round can cost a whole round of finality.
07 One-Slot Glitch at a Round Start.setup: 4 nodes, 64 honest validators, 200 ms latency. A one-slot 50/50 cut at slot 48, the first slot of round 6.
07 One-Slot Glitch at a Round Start.result: The confirmation update of slot 48 sees only 32 votes on every node, so no node has a block to give the finality gadget and nobody attests in round 6. The round is lost for finality: the step due at slot 50 comes at slot 58. The same cut at slot 49 costs one slot.

08 Half the Network Asleep.goal: Check liveness and recovery when half of the validators go offline.
08 Half the Network Asleep.setup: 4 nodes, 64 honest validators, 200 ms latency. Nodes 2 and 3 (32 validators) are asleep for slots 48–63.
08 Half the Network Asleep.result: The awake half keeps confirming and slow-locks, but 32 is below the quorum of 43, so finality stalls. The sleepers restart, rejoin within a slot, and finality resumes a round later.

09 Silent Adversary.goal: Set the baseline for the adversary tabs: a faulty third of the validators that does nothing.
09 Silent Adversary.setup: 4 nodes; 43 honest validators (11/11/10/11) and 21 faulty ones (33%) run by one adversary; 200 ms latency. The adversary never votes, proposes or attests.
09 Silent Adversary.result: Its proposer slots stay empty. The 43 honest validators are exactly the quorum, so finality needs every one of them, and gets it.

10 Equivocating Adversary.goal: Check whether double votes and double blocks from a faulty third break confirmation or finality.
10 Equivocating Adversary.setup: 4 nodes; 43 honest validators (11/11/10/11) and 21 faulty ones (33%) run by one adversary; 200 ms latency. Every slot each faulty validator votes for two conflicting heads, one to each half of the network; at its proposer slots the adversary proposes two blocks.
10 Equivocating Adversary.result: Honest nodes relay both copies, so every node sees the equivocations within Δ and excludes the equivocators from confirmation and unlocking. Nothing breaks.

11 Two-Faced Adversary Across a Cut.goal: Check whether an adversary can use a partition to break safety after it heals.
11 Two-Faced Adversary Across a Cut.setup: 4 nodes; 43 honest validators (11/11/10/11) and 21 faulty ones (33%) run by one adversary; 200 ms latency. Nodes 0–1 and 2–3 are cut apart for slots 48–63; the adversary acts honestly on both sides at once, and releases the blocks it kept back after the heal.
11 Two-Faced Adversary Across a Cut.result: Side A plus the adversary reaches the quorum and finalizes on its own during the cut (allowed before GST). Finality resumes 10 slots after the heal and nothing breaks. The same holds across 2,304 seeded runs of this kind.

12 Finalization Hiding.goal: Break a confirmed, fast-locked block under synchrony with a faulty minority: make some honest nodes confirm a block that is then orphaned. This version needs proposer equivocation; tab 15 removes it.
12 Finalization Hiding.setup: Synchrony throughout: every message and every relay arrives within 200 ms, one clock, everything relayed. 21 of 64 validators faulty, run by one adversary; it targets nodes 0–2. The adversary proposes slots 33 and 34, right after the round's attestations.
12 Finalization Hiding.how:
• Slot 33: block B reaches nodes 0 and 3 just before their vote; with 10 early faulty votes it has exactly 32 = n/2 early votes. 11 faulty votes are kept back.
  • Slot 34, three adversary blocks: FB extends B and carries the round's attestations (to nodes 0–2 only); Q forks below the block FB finalizes and carries the 11 hidden votes; Z is a sibling of B (to node 3).
  • Nodes 0–2 finalize through FB, so they refuse Q and never count its votes: they see 53 voters, where node 3 sees 64.
12 Finalization Hiding.result: Nodes 0–2 confirm and fast-lock B at slot 34 (32 of 53 voters). Node 3 does not (32 of 64) and votes Z. In slot 35 Z's 32 votes move the locks back and B is orphaned, after being shown as confirmed for 4.5 s. Needs proposer equivocation (three blocks in slot 34).

13 Finalization Hiding, Strict Fast Test.goal: Check whether a strict fast test (more than n/2 support instead of n/2 or more, not the spec) stops the finalization-hiding attack of tab 12.
13 Finalization Hiding, Strict Fast Test.setup: Synchrony throughout: every message and every relay arrives within 200 ms, one clock, everything relayed. 21 of 64 validators faulty, run by one adversary; it targets nodes 0–2. As tab 12, with the strict test; the adversary sends its Z votes only to the slot-35 proposer.
13 Finalization Hiding, Strict Fast Test.result: Nodes 0–2 write no lock, but 32 of 53 voters is still a strict majority, so they still confirm B, for 3–4.5 s, before it is orphaned. Over 74 attacked schedules: 74 succeed when the Z votes arrive just before the view freeze (B shown for 1.5 s), 48 with this proposer-only variant. The strict test protects locks, not the confirmed tip.

14 Finalization Hiding, Refused-Votes Fi.goal: Check a fix for the finalization-hiding attack of tab 12: count the votes a block carries even when the block itself is refused.
14 Finalization Hiding, Refused-Votes Fi.setup: Synchrony throughout: every message and every relay arrives within 200 ms, one clock, everything relayed. 21 of 64 validators faulty, run by one adversary; it targets nodes 0–2. As tab 12, with the fix (not the spec).
14 Finalization Hiding, Refused-Votes Fi.result: Nodes 0–2 count Q's 11 hidden votes too, so B has 32 of 64 voters everywhere and nobody confirms it. Nothing is orphaned. The fix closes every variant with either threshold (0 of 74 attacked schedules). Tab 17 shows the other fix, forwarding the carried votes, which the live spec adopted.

zooms: s44: FB and Q; B confirmed
15 Finalization Hiding Without Equivocat.goal: Break a confirmed, fast-locked block under synchrony with a faulty minority, as in tab 12, but without proposer equivocation: one block per slot and one vote per validator, nothing slashable.
15 Finalization Hiding Without Equivocat.setup: Synchrony throughout: every message and every relay arrives within 200 ms, one clock, everything relayed. 21 of 64 validators faulty, run by one adversary; it targets nodes 0–2. The adversary proposes slots 42, 43 and 44.
15 Finalization Hiding Without Equivocat.how:
• Slot 42: FB, on the honest head W, carries the round's attestations; kept back.
  • Slot 43: B, on W, reaches nodes 0–2 just before their vote: 32 honest votes, exactly n/2. The 21 faulty votes (for W) are kept back.
  • Slot 44: Q forks below the block FB finalizes and carries the 21 hidden votes. Q reaches node 3 just before its vote; FB reaches nodes 0–2 just before theirs, so they refuse Q.
  • From slot 45 the faulty validators vote W: 32 (nodes 0–2, locked on B) against 11 + 21 = 32, so B never regains a majority.
15 Finalization Hiding Without Equivocat.result: Nodes 0–2 confirm and fast-lock B at slot 44 (32 of 43 voters) and show it as confirmed for 22.5 s, until the lock expires in slot 48 and B is orphaned. The tie also orphans the honest blocks of slots 47 and 48. Works in 138 of 138 attacked schedules.

16 Without Equivocation, First-Seen Goss.goal: Check whether Ethereum's gossip rule, which ignores a proposer's second block for a slot, stops the finalization-hiding attack without equivocation of tab 15. (It stops the version with equivocation, tab 12.)
16 Without Equivocation, First-Seen Goss.setup: Synchrony throughout: every message and every relay arrives within 200 ms, one clock, everything relayed. 21 of 64 validators faulty, run by one adversary; it targets nodes 0–2. As tab 15, under Ethereum's rule: a node ignores a proposer's second block for a slot and relays only the first copy of each vote.
16 Without Equivocation, First-Seen Goss.result: Nothing changes: the attack has one block per slot and one vote per validator. Nodes 0–2 show B as confirmed for 22.5 s, as in tab 15. The attack with equivocation (tab 12) fails under this rule.

17 Without Equivocation, Vote Forwarding.goal: Check whether the live spec's new rule, forwarding the votes carried by every accepted block, closes the finalization-hiding attack without equivocation of tab 15.
17 Without Equivocation, Vote Forwarding.setup: Synchrony throughout: every message and every relay arrives within 200 ms, one clock, everything relayed. 21 of 64 validators faulty, run by one adversary; it targets nodes 0–2. As tab 15, with the rule of the live Goldilocks spec (ethlabs-org/eth-consensus-lean, Nov 2026): an honest node forwards the votes it admits from an accepted block, whether or not other nodes accept that block.
17 Without Equivocation, Vote Forwarding.result: Node 3 accepts Q and forwards its 21 hidden votes, which reach nodes 0–2 before their confirmation update. Every node counts 64 voters, so nobody confirms B and no honest block is orphaned. It holds by design: an honest node votes by +Δ, the update runs at +2Δ, and forwarding takes less than Δ.

18 Finalization Hiding, Slow Attestation.goal: Measure how much cheaper the finalization-hiding attack without equivocation (tab 15) gets when attestations are slower than blocks, as they are in practice because attestations are most of the traffic.
18 Finalization Hiding, Slow Attestation.setup: Synchrony throughout: every message and every relay arrives within 200 ms, one clock, everything relayed. 21 of 64 validators faulty, run by one adversary; it targets nodes 0–2. Attestations take up to Δ<sub>F</sub> = 8Δ = 12 s (the spec only asks Δ<sub>F</sub> ≥ Δ). The adversary delays every honest attestation of the round as far as that allows.
18 Finalization Hiding, Slow Attestation.how: No honest proposer can finalize before the delayed attestations land, so FB can be the adversary's block from any earlier slot of the round: here slot 42, built late. Slot 43 is honest; B is slot 44 and Q slot 45.
18 Finalization Hiding, Slow Attestation.result: Nodes 0–2 confirm and lock B and show it for 22.5 s before it is orphaned. The attack needs B and Q consecutive plus one earlier adversary slot: about 11% of rounds qualify at 8Δ, against 4% at Δ.

19 Late Justification Contest.goal: Check whether an adversary can trigger a finality contest (a justification on a branch that newer blocks do not extend), and whether the contest hurts.
19 Late Justification Contest.setup: 4 nodes; 43 honest validators (11/11/10/11) and 21 faulty ones (33%) run by one adversary; 200 ms latency. Nodes 0–1 and 2–3 are cut apart for slots 50–57, over a finality action. The faulty validators side with each half, and justify side A's checkpoint inside a block they keep (slot 62).
19 Late Justification Contest.result: After the heal everyone follows side B. At slot 68 the adversary reveals the kept block: every node holds a justification on a branch its newer blocks do not extend, a contest, for 6 slots (68–73). It is harmless: the spec's rule and the Lean model's give the same outcome, and the round of finality lost comes from the split itself (the same run without the reveal loses it too).

20 Outage of 3 Slots.goal: Measure how long a period of asynchrony a fast confirmation survives: here an outage of 3 slots, the longest the Lean proof covers for this timing. Tab 21 goes just beyond it.
20 Outage of 3 Slots.setup: 4 nodes; 43 honest validators (11/11/10/11) and 21 faulty ones (33%) run by one adversary; 200 ms latency. The honest block B of slot 44 is confirmed and fast-locked everywhere at slot 45. Then every node is cut off from every other for 3 slots (from slot 47), while the adversary votes for a sibling of B.
20 Outage of 3 Slots.result: Every node keeps B after the heal. 3 slots is exactly the Lean proof's bound for this timing.

21 Outage of 3.75 Slots.goal: Measure how long a period of asynchrony a fast confirmation survives: here an outage of 3.75 slots, just beyond the Lean proof's bound. Tab 20 stays within it.
21 Outage of 3.75 Slots.setup: 4 nodes; 43 honest validators (11/11/10/11) and 21 faulty ones (33%) run by one adversary; 200 ms latency. The honest block B of slot 44 is confirmed and fast-locked everywhere at slot 45. Then every node is cut off from every other for 3.75 slots (from slot 47), while the adversary votes for a sibling of B.
21 Outage of 3.75 Slots.result: After the heal the sibling wins: every node drops B, after showing it as confirmed for 36 s. The Lean bound is tight: the real tolerance is between 3 and 3.75 slots, depending on where the outage starts in the slot.
